lines: Eight-channel stereo mixer with a pan, a mute, a solo and a level CV on every channel, and a master fader
Sets the level of that channel, marked from +6dB down to silence and starting at 0dB, the gain being the square of the fader position
Pans that channel between the two outputs; at the centre both outputs carry it at full level, and moving it to one side attenuates the far output while the near one stays full
Switches that channel in and out of the mix, the level ramping over about five samples rather than jumping
Solos that channel; while any solo on the module is on, only soloed channels reach the outputs
The signal for that channel, read as a single monophonic voltage
Voltage control of that channel's level: the channel is multiplied by this voltage divided by 10, so 10V passes it at the fader setting and 0V silences it
Sets the level of the whole mix, marked from +6dB down to silence and starting at 0dB
The left side of the mix
The right side of the mix
Menu — DC block puts a DC blocking filter on each channel
StereoMixer-8.notes: The pan law was read from the module's process code in the installed 2.1.4 binary: the parameter runs 0 to 2 and is displayed as -100% to +100%, and at the centre both outputs are fed at full level rather than the usual 3dB down. The level CV multiplies the channel by volts divided by 10 and is not attenuated, so anything above 10V makes the channel louder than the fader setting.

StereoMixer-8-2.notes: The aux send knobs and the pan CV attenuators share the same places on the panel, and so do the aux 2 send knobs and the track routing buttons: the widget shows one set or the other according to the display button and the matching menu item, so only one of each pair can be clicked at a time. Both are given lines. The panel prints INSERT 1 - 8 and the code sets eight channels on the insert output, which agrees. Parameters 77 and 78 are named Group 1 and Group 2 by the maker but the code passes them to a group solo check, which is why their line calls them solo.

StereoMixer-16-2.notes: Channels 13 to 16 are stereo and take two jacks each, printed L and R; that is why there are twenty audio inputs for sixteen channels. The panel prints INSERT 1 - 12 but the process code in the installed 2.1.4 binary sets eight channels on the insert output, so only the first eight channels are actually sent; the insert output's own line says so. The aux send knobs share their places with the pan CV attenuators, and the aux 2 send knobs with the track routing buttons, the display button choosing which set is shown; both are given lines. Parameters 149 to 152 are named Group 1 to Group 4 by the maker but the code passes them to a group solo check.
